detailed_findings.finding: The residue-class decomposition is correct and sufficient to compute the complement cardinality.
The proof fully justifies that in residue class i, S_x contains exactly the terms i+tm with t >= x_i.
The observation that the stated inequalities on x are unused is acceptable here, since the genus formula follows solely from the definition of S_x.

reason: The proof correctly characterizes, for each residue class modulo m, exactly which elements lie in S_x and which do not. In residue class 0 all multiples of m are included, and in residue class i\in{1,...,m-1} the included elements are exactly {i+tm : t\ge x_i}, so the missing ones are exactly {i+tm : 0\le t < x_i}, giving x_i missing elements. Since residue classes are disjoint, summing yields |N0 \\ S_x| = \sum_i x_i. This matches the lemma statement exactly. The Kunz inequalities are indeed unused for this counting lemma, but that is not a defect since the claim depends only on the explicit form of S_x.
